STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r2.speaker: Al, IJ
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r2.claim: Al and IJ consider verses 163–167 to have been revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r2.anchor:
Some,
however, have considered vv. 163–67 to have been revealed in
Madinah (Al, IJ).

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.claim: The discussion returns to the Israelites' later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer for it.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.anchor: the Israelites’ later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer as a result (vv. 159–71)

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r1.claim: The common reading has معذرة in the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: our admonition is an excuse.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة " معذرة " رفعا على خبر ابتداء مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وزيد ابن علي وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r2.claim: These readers use the accusative, for which three syntactic analyses are offered.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r2.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم وزيد ابن علي وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r3.claim: The strongest accusative analysis makes the word a purpose complement: they admonished the people to make an excuse before God; Sībawayh confirms this usage.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r3.anchor: أظهرها: أنها منصوبة على المفعول من أجله، أي: وعظناه لأجل المعذرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r4.claim: A second accusative analysis treats it as a cognate accusative, with an implied verb meaning we apologize an apology.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r4.anchor: الثاني: أنها منصوبة على المصدر بفعل مقدر من لفظها تقديره: نعتذر معذرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r5.claim: A third analysis treats it as the object of saying because the verbal noun entails speech, as in قلت خطبة.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r5.anchor: انتصاب المفعول به لأن المعذرة تتضمن كلاما

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r6.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r6.claim: Sībawayh prefers nominative: they were not beginning a separate apology but answering that their admonition itself was their excuse.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r6.anchor: وسيـبويه يختار الرفع قال: " لأنهم لم يريدوا أن يعتذروا

SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r7.speaker: الأزهري
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r7.claim: Al-Azharī says معذرة means الاعتذار; العذر is disavowal of a sin.
SAMIN-DURR:7:164/r7.anchor: قال الأزهري: " إنها بمعنى الاعتذار " والعذر: التنصل من الذنب

ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r8.claim: Limā originally has an alif; Arabic deletes that alif after prepositions, as in famā and ʿam.
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r8.anchor: الأصل لما، ولكن الألف تحذف مع حروف الجر نحو لم وعم وبم

ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r9.claim: The questioners reproached the admonishers because they thought the people would not desist; that was their predominant assessment of the people.
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r9.anchor: ومعنى الآية أنهم لاموهم في عظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين. هذا الأغلب عليهم في العلم بهم

ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r10.claim: Given what they saw of the people's deeds, the admonishers said the people would inevitably be destroyed in this world or severely punished in the next.
ZAJJAJ:v2p384/r10.anchor: أعمالهم - أنهم مهلكون في الدنيا أو معذبون في الآخرة لا محالة

ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r1.claim: They mean that admonishing the people is their excuse before God; commanding right is incumbent on them, and the people might benefit and become mindful.
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r1.anchor: قالوا موعظتنا إياهم معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r2.claim: Maʿdhiratan may be accusative as a verbal noun, meaning that they apologize with an apology.
ZAJJAJ:v2p385/r2.anchor: ويجوز النصب في " معذرة " فيكون المعنى

ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n130/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n130/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n130/r1.claim: The community asking why the Sabbath-breakers are admonished comprised passive bystanders who neither protested nor themselves profaned the Sabbath.
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n130/r1.anchor: people who, while not actively protesting against the impiety of their environment, did not themselves participate in this profanation of the Sabbath.

ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n131/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n131/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n131/r1.claim: The people who answer are the truly pious among the community, like those described in 7:159.
ASAD-NOTES:7:163#n131/r1.anchor: the really pious among them, such as are described in verse 159 above.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r1.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r1.claim: Abū Zayd gives the related forms عذرته، أعذره، عذرا، معذرة، and عذرى for excusing or making an excuse.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r1.anchor: قال أبو زيد: عذرته. أعذره عذرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r2.claim: These six readers use the nominative معذرة; Abū Bakr’s route through Yaḥyā ibn Ādam from ʿĀṣim also has the nominative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع، وأبو عمرو، وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي معذرة رفعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r3.claim: The nominative is parsed on the model of حنان in the cited line, as an initial nominal expression rather than a verbal object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r3.anchor: أن سيبويه قال: ومثله [في قراءته] على الابتداء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r4.speaker: الحسين بن علي الجعفي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r4.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī’s route from Abū Bakr and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read معذرة in the accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p97/r4.anchor: وروى الحسين بن علي الجعفي عن أبي بكر وحفص عن عاصم معذرة نصبا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r1.claim: Rafʿ can mean our admonition is an excuse, with an omitted subject, or can posit an omitted demonstrative as in this is a sūra.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأه بالرفع أنه أراد أحد وجهين من العربية إما أن يكون أراد قالوا موعظتنا إياهم معذرة فتكون خبر إبتداء محذوف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r2.claim: Naṣb answers why they admonish: they do so as an apology and excuse.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p166/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أن الكلام جواب كأنه قيل لهم لم تعظون قوما هذه سبيلهم قالوا نعظهم اعتذارا ومعذرة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ معذرة ﴾ بالرفع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r2.speaker: عاصم عن أبي بكر، حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r2.claim: Abū Bakr via Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and others reports nominative from ʿĀṣim; Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī from Abū Bakr and Ḥafṣ report accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p296/r2.anchor: واختلف عن عاصم فروى أبو بكر فى رواية يحيى بن آدم عنه وغيره ﴿ معذرة ﴾ رفعا

QIRAAT-ER:7:164:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:164:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:164:16#1/r1.claim: The nominative maʿdhiratun can be a predicate, it is an exculpation, or a subject, an exculpation is our motive, rather than accusative.
QIRAAT-ER:7:164:16#1/r1.anchor: Nominative reading (marfūʿ with tanwīn) — shifts from accusative ḥāl/mafʿūl to nominative predicate

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas counts three groups: those who admonished, those admonished, and those who objected to admonishing; he says God knows what the third group did.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم ﴾ قال قال ابن عباس هم ثلاث فرق الفرقة التي وعظت والموعوظة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi offers a two-group account: the admonishers and the people who said, “Why admonish a people?”; he identifies the latter with the admonished group.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p239#2/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال الكلبي هما فرقتان الفرقة التي وعظت والتي قالت ﴿ لم تعظون قوما ﴾ هي الموعوظة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r1.claim: One account has three groups, with the questioners asking why admonish only after repeated warnings failed; another has two groups, and the obedient ask this among themselves after seeing no effect.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r2.claim: The majority read معذرة in the nominative: their admonition is an excuse before God, avoids blame for neglecting the duty to forbid wrongdoing, and holds out hope of reform.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور معذرة بالرفع أي موعظتنا إقامة عذر إلى الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي وعاصم وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r3.claim: These readers have the accusative, meaning that they admonished the people as an excuse; Abū Ḥayyān says Sībawayh prefers the nominative in this context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وعاصم في بعض ما روي عنه وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف معذرة بالنصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r4.claim: Sībawayh allows نصب in an independent apology, but prefers رفع here because the speakers answer that their admonition itself is an excuse, rather than begin a new apology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه: لو قال رجل لرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses the accusative as a purpose object; another analysis treats it as a verbal noun meaning we apologize.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p208/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: من نصب فعلى المفعول له

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r1.claim: The opening connects to the earlier account of Sabbath transgression, showing persistence despite admonitions and warnings.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r1.anchor: عطف على إذ يعدون مسوق لبيان تماديهم في العدوان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r2.speaker: الطيبي والتفتازاني
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r2.claim: Al-Ṭībī and al-Taftāzānī reject attaching it to the closer ‘when they came’: that would include the questioners among Sabbath transgressors.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r2.anchor: الطيبي والتفتازاني : ولايجوز أن يكون معطوفا على إذ تأتيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r3.claim: The temporal reading makes the argument clear; the substitute reading fails because the saying followed rather than coincided with transgression, and treating the period as an extended year is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r3.anchor: أن زمان القول بعد زمان العدوان ومغاير له

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r4.claim: The group are righteous people who had not spared effort in admonishing; once they despaired of acceptance, they persisted in hope of benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r4.anchor: جماعة من صلحائهم الذين لم يألوا جهدا في عظتهم حين يئسوا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r5.claim: Destroying them means uprooting them from earth; the alternative is severe punishment short of extermination, or destruction in this world versus punishment in the next.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r5.anchor: أي مستأصلهم بالكلية ومطهر وجه الأرض منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r6.claim: On the world-or-afterlife reading, ‘or’ prevents exclusion, and the active participles present the outcomes as certain and virtually occurring.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r6.anchor: إيثار صيغة اسم الفاعل في الشقين للدلالة على تحقيق كل من الإهلاك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r7.claim: They ask why rather than directly command ‘do not admonish’ because the apparent futility is astonishing, or to ask about the advice’s wisdom and benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r7.anchor: مبالغة في أن الوعظ لاينجع فيهم إذ المقصود لاتعظوا أو أتعظون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r8.claim: The question may have been an exchange among righteous preachers, one asking why they continued an ineffectual task.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r8.anchor: هذا تقاول وقع بين الصلحاء الواعظين كأنه قال بعضهم لبعض

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r9.claim: Either group of questioners may have spoken in the sinners’ presence to encourage repentance, since a firm prediction of doom may instill fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r9.anchor: ويحتمل على كلا القولين أن ذلك صدر من القائل بمحصر من القوم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r10.claim: A further view makes the Sabbath violators the speakers, mocking the warners, but the commentator considers this unlikely.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r11.claim: ‘As an excuse’ may be a purpose complement to admonishing, an absolute object after an omitted verb, or an object of ‘they said’ denoting apology.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r11.anchor: نعظهم معذرة إليه تعالى على أنه مفعول له

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r12.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r12.claim: Maʿdhira originally means excuse or clearing oneself from sin; al-Azharī glosses it as apology, and ‘to’ reflects conveying it to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r12.anchor: وقال الأزهري : إنه بمعنى الاعتذار وعداه بإلى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r13.claim: Calling God ‘your Lord’ indirectly rebukes the questioners; on the literal reading, the reply wisely redirects from the expected answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r13.anchor: إضافة الرب إلى ضمير المخاطبين نوع تعريض بالسائلين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r14.speaker: من عدا حفص والمفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r14.claim: All readers except Ḥafṣ and al-Mufaḍḍal read the word in the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: ‘our admonition is an excuse.’
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r14.anchor: من عدا حفص والمفضل ( معذرة ) بالرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r15.claim: The clause coordinates with ‘as an excuse,’ expressing hope that they attain at least some piety.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r15.anchor: عطف على معذرة أي ورجاء أن يتقوا بعض التقاة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r16.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r16.claim: Shaykh al-Islām says the wording explicitly shows the questioners are not part of the doomed group.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p91/r16.anchor: شيخ الإسلام : وهذا صريح في أن القائلين لم تعظون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p92/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p92/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p92/r1.claim: To preserve the view that questioners were Sabbath violators, one may posit a shift in address or wording patterned on their calling themselves ‘a people’; both depart from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p92/r1.anchor: القول بأنه إلتفات أو مشاكلة لتعبيرهم عن أنفسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the questioners as members of the doomed faction, who answered warnings that God would punish them by asking why they were being admonished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.anchor: اختلفوا في الذين قالوا هذا، قيل: كانوا من الفرقة الهالكة، وذلك أنهم لما قيل لهم انتهوا عن هذا العمل السيئ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.claim: The aw may be understood as asking whether they knew God would punish the people severely.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.claim: The answer maʿdhira means that their admonition serves as an excuse before their Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.anchor: ومعناه أن الأمر بالمعروف واجب علينا فعلينا موعظة هؤلاء عذرا إلى الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.speaker: حفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.claim: Hafs reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative, meaning we do this as an excuse to your Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حفص: "معذرة" بالنصب أي نفعل ذلك معذرة إلى ربكم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.claim: The stronger view is that the quiet faction asks why they admonish, and the enjoiners answer that commanding right is obligatory and their advice excuses them before God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.anchor: والأصح أنها من قول الفرقة الساكنة، قالوا لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم، قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم، ومعناه أن الأمر بالمعروف واجب علينا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.claim: They hope the wrongdoers will fear God and abandon sin; if the address were to the violators, it would say laʿallakum.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.anchor: {ولعلهم يتقون} أي: يتقون الله ويتركوا المعصية، ولو كان الخطاب مع المعتدين لكان يقول ولعلكم تتقون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r1.claim: The time clause is coordinated with the earlier mention of when the Sabbath-breakers transgressed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r1.anchor: وإذ قالت } عطف على { إذ يعدون }

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r2.claim: The group are the town's righteous people, who persisted in admonishing until they despaired of the others taking heed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r2.anchor: جماعة من أهل القرية يعني صلحاءهم الذين اجتهدوا في موعظتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r3.claim: The questioners may be overstating that admonition cannot help, asking why the admonishers continue, or speaking as a reformed group to those who have not reformed; another view makes them members of the doomed faction responding mockingly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r3.anchor: قالوه مبالغة في أن الوعظ لا ينفع فيهم، أو سؤالا عن علة الوعظ ونفعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r4.claim: Muhl ikuhum here means that God will destroy or annihilate them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r4.anchor: لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم } مخترمهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r5.claim: The severe punishment is in the afterlife because of their persistent disobedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r6.claim: The advisers answer that they warn people to establish their excuse before God and avoid being accused of neglecting the duty to forbid wrong.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r6.anchor: موعظتنا إنهاء عذر إلى الله حتى لا ننسب إلى تفريط في النهي عن المنكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r7.speaker: حفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative, as a verbal noun or causal expression: they offered an excuse or admonished as their excuse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r7.anchor: وقرأ حفص { معذرة } بالنصب على المصدر أو العلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r8.claim: They hope the sinners will desist; despair of their reform only comes with their destruction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:164/r8.anchor: إذ اليأس لا يحصل إلا بالهلاك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r1.claim: The account confirms that persistent sin is the community's habit, continuing the account of their Sabbath transgression in 7:163.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r2.claim: The questioning group is a community of righteous admonishers who had persisted in warning until they despaired of another group that would not desist.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r2.anchor: جماعة ممن يعتبر ويقصد من الواعظين الصالحين الذين وعظوا حتى أيسوا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r3.claim: The questioners ask why they keep admonishing people expected to be destroyed or severely punished for their persistent corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r3.anchor: لا يقلعون عن الوعظ تخوفا للموعوظين بما ينجاوزن به

BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r4.claim: The admonishers answer that they warn to have an excuse before their Lord: if asked about the sinners, they can say they made every effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r4.anchor: أي المحسن إليكم بالحفظ عما وقعوا فيه من الذنب والإقبال على الوعظ

BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r5.claim: Their other hope is that the warnings might make the sinners fear God and turn back from their wrongdoing.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p140/r5.anchor: وليكون حالهم حال من يرجى خوفه لله فيرجع عن غيه

BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r5.claim: The episode is linked by coordination to the earlier account of their Sabbath transgression.

BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r6.claim: The preaching group were righteous people who persisted in admonishing with every effort despite losing hope that others would accept, both to fulfill their duty and in hope of benefit.
BURSEVI:v3p201#2/r6.anchor: جماعة من صلحائهم الذين ركبوا في عظتهم متن كل صعب وذلول

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r1.claim: The question asks why they admonish a people whom God will surely destroy or punish severely.

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r2.claim: Muhlikuhum means to eradicate them and cleanse the land of them.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r2.anchor: {الله مهلكهم} أي : مستأصلهم ومطهر الأرض منهم

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r3.claim: The alternative means punishing them severely without completely eradicating them.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r3.anchor: {أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} دون الاستئصال بالمرة

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r4.claim: The questioners mean a worldly punishment and argue that preaching cannot succeed; they are not rejecting admonition or approving the sinners' conduct.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r4.anchor: والمفهوم من بقية الآية كون المراد عذاب

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r5.claim: The phrase functions as a purpose complement: the preachers admonish in order to offer an excuse to their Lord.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r5.anchor: {قالوا} أي : الوعاظ {معذرة إلى ربكم} مفعول له

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r6.claim: Muʿdhira is a verbal noun meaning excuse: a person seeks to erase sin by denying an act, explaining why it was done, or promising not to repeat it; that last case is repentance, and every repentance is an excuse but not vice versa.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r6.anchor: والمعذرة : اسم مصدر بمعنى العذر وهو بضم فسكون في الأصل

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, muʿdhira means apologizing; the verb is used with min, and an apologizer may be either right or wrong.

BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r8.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r8.claim: Al-Saʿdī's verses contrast a stern address at the gathering with the chance to offer an excuse and hope for forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v3p201#3/r8.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : كر بمحشر خطاب قهر كند

BURSEVI:v3p202/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p202/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p202/r1.claim: He coordinates the hope of their becoming mindful with the excuse: they may acquire some piety and stop sinning, since rational people may accept clear truth.
BURSEVI:v3p202/r1.anchor: عطف على معذرة ، أي : ورجاء لأن يتقوا بعض التقاة ويتركوا المعصية

BURSEVI:v3p202/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p202/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p202/r2.claim: The questioners were not among the doomed: despair requires certainty of destruction, and otherwise the admonishers would have said “perhaps you may be mindful.”
BURSEVI:v3p202/r2.anchor: واليأس لا يحصل إلا بالهلاك وهذا صريح في أن القائلين لم تعظون إلخ ليسوا من الفرقة الهالكة

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r1.claim: The account distinguishes those who preached, those who criticized the preaching, and the Sabbath violators; it says both groups who spoke were saved, while the violators were turned into apes.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r1.anchor: فقالت طائفة من النهاة: تعلمون أن هؤلاء قوم قد حق عليهم العذاب {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم}

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God had prescribed Friday for Israel, but they chose Saturday; the Sabbath became a test when fish came visibly to Aylah, Midian, and al-Tur on Saturdays and disappeared afterward.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {واسألهم عن القرية} الآية قال: إن الله إنما افترض على بني إسرائيل اليوم الذي افترض عليكم يوم الجمعة فخالفوا إلى يوم السبت

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that one man secretly tied a Saturday fish to a stake and retrieved it the next day; others copied the ploy until the Sabbath violation became public, while only a remnant admonished them.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r3.anchor: ثم إن رجلا منهم أخذ حوتا فحزمه بخيط ثم ضرب له وتدا في الساحل وربطه وتركه في الماء فلما كان الغد جاء فأخذه

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the three groups were the warners, those who asked why they admonished a people destined for punishment, and the Sabbath violators; he says only the warners escaped and the rest were destroyed.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r4.anchor: فكانوا أثلاثا ثلثا نهى وثلثا قالوا {لم تعظون} وثلثا أصحاب الخطيئة فما نجا إلا الذين نهوا وهلك سائرهم

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r5.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, the warning is an excuse before God and a hope that the offenders might stop and become mindful.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r5.anchor: قالوا {معذرة إلى ربكم} في سخطنا أعمالهم {ولعلهم يتقون}

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the spared warners found the doors shut, discovered the offenders transformed into apes, and recognized them individually by their faces.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r6.anchor: فاطلعوا في دورهم فإذا القوم قد مسخوا يعرفون الرجل بعينه وأنه لقرد والمرأة بعينها وانها لقردة

DURR-FULL:v3p588/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r7.claim: Ikrima recalls finding Ibn Abbas weeping over the Qur'an and identifying the pages that moved him as these leaves.
DURR-FULL:v3p588/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: جئت ابن عباس يوما وهو يبكي وإذا المصحف في حجره فقلت: ما يبكيك يا ابن عباس فقال: هؤلاء الورقات

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r1.claim: Continuing Ikrima's account, Ibn Abbas asks whether he knows Aylah and describes its Jews, whose fish appeared in abundance on Saturdays and vanished afterward.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r1.anchor: وإذا في سورة الأعراف قال: تعرف أيلة قلت: نعم قال: فإنه كان بها حي من يهود سيقت الحيتان إليهم يوم السبت

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fish were white and fat like pregnant camels; Satan persuaded some Jews that they could catch them on Saturday if they ate them on another day, while others said both catching and eating were forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r2.anchor: وكانت تأتيهم يوم السبت شرعا بيضا سمانا كأنها الماخض فكانوا كذلك برهة من الدهر ثم إن الشيطان أوحى إليهم

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the righteous group separating from the violators and warning them; the group that questioned the warnings asked why they admonished people God would destroy, and the warners answered that they sought an excuse before God and hoped the people would stop.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r3.anchor: وسكتت وقال الأيمنون: ويلكم لا تتعرضوا لعقوبة الله وقال الأيسرون {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا}

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r4.claim: The admonishers say they warn as an excuse before God and because they prefer that the sinners stop and escape punishment.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r4.anchor: قال الأيمنون: {معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون} ان ينتهوا فهو أحب إلينا أن لا يصابوا ولا يهلكوا

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r5.claim: After the offenders persisted, the warners vowed to separate from them, warned that God would punish them, and found the next morning that the doors were shut and the townspeople had become apes.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r5.anchor: فمضوا على الخطيئة وقال الأيمنون: قد فعلتم يا أعداء الله والله لنبايننكم الليلة في مدينتكم

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r6.claim: The transformed apes recognized their human relatives, approached them weeping, and nodded yes when asked whether the people had warned them.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r6.anchor: فعرفت القردة أنسابها من الانس ولا تعرف الانس أنسابها من القردة فجعلت القرود تأتي نسيبها من الانس

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the text mentions the saved warners but not the silent group; he observes that people still witness wrongdoing without speaking, while Ikrima objects that the silent group disliked it and opposed the offenders.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r8.anchor: قال: فارى الذين نهوا قد نجوا ولا أرى الآخرين ذكروا ونحن نرى أشياء ننكرها ولا نقول فيها

DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r9.claim: Ikrima challenges Ibn Abbas that the other group also disliked the wrongdoing and opposed the sinners; Ibn Abbas then ordered that he be given two coarse garments.
DURR-FULL:v3p588#2/r9.anchor: قلت: أي جعلني الله فداك ألا ترى أنهم كرهوا ما هم عليه وخالفوهم وقالوا {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} قال: فأمر بي فكسيت ثوبين غليظين

DURR-FULL:v3p589/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r1.claim: Ikrima says Aylah had two stone idols, Laqim and Laqmana, and God directed fish to come to them on Saturdays while the people were told not to touch the fish that day.
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: كانت قرية على ساحل البحر يقال لها ايلة وكان على ساحل البحر صنمان من حجارة مستقبلان الماء يقال لأحدهما لقيم والآخر لقمانة

DURR-FULL:v3p589/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that fish appeared within reach on Saturdays; the villagers decided to catch them that day and eat them Sunday, and more fish appeared on subsequent Saturdays.
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r2.anchor: فكان إذا طلع الفجر يوم السبت أقبل السمك شرعا إلى الصنمين لا يمتنع من آخذ يأخذه

DURR-FULL:v3p589/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r3.claim: When the Sabbath violation spread, some warned the people and others asked why they admonished a community God would destroy; the warners said they sought an excuse before God and hoped the people would stop.
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r3.anchor: فقام آخرون فقالوا {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون}

DURR-FULL:v3p589/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r4.claim: Ikrima says the warners refused to spend the night in the town with the offenders; the next morning the closed houses held apes, from small to large, male and female.
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r4.anchor: فقام الذين نهوا عن السوء فقالوا: لا نبيت معكم الليلة في هذه القرية

DURR-FULL:v3p589/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r5.claim: The apes recognized particular people and nodded yes when called by name; the warners then opened the doors, and the apes fled to the wilderness.
DURR-FULL:v3p589/r5.anchor: فدخلوا عليهم فإذا هم قردة كلهم فجعل الرجل يومىء إلى القرد منهم أنت فلان فيومىء برأسه: نعم

DURR-FULL:v3p590/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Sabbath admonishers were saved, its perpetrators perished, and he did not know what became of the silent group.
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نجا الناهون وهلك الفاعلون

DURR-FULL:v3p590/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas wished the questioners had been saved with those who forbade evil, but feared the punishment may have descended on all.
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: والله لئن أكون علمت أن القوم الذين قالوا {لم تعظون قوما}

DURR-FULL:v3p590/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas first did not know whether the questioners escaped; he later learned they were saved and gave his informant a robe.
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: قال ابن عباس:

DURR-FULL:v3p590/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r4.speaker: ليث بن أبي سليم
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r4.claim: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym reports that the questioners were turned to stone.
DURR-FULL:v3p590/r4.anchor: عن ليث بن أبي سليم قال: مسخوا حجارة الذين قالوا {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم}

DURR-FULL:v3p591/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p591/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد العزيز العمري
DURR-FULL:v3p591/r7.claim: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Umari says enjoining right remains an excuse before God even when the addressee will not accept.
DURR-FULL:v3p591/r7.anchor: عن سفيان قال: قالوا لعبد الله بن عبد العزيز العمري

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Sabbath offenders tethering fish in the water, retrieving and eating them secretly the next day; only some kept warning them until the practice became public.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ثم ان رجلا منهم اخذ حوتا فخرمه بخيط ، ثم ضرب له وتدا في الساحل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan suggested that only eating fish on Saturday was forbidden, so one group caught it that day and ate it later.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ثم ان الشيطان اوحى اليهم فقال : انما نهيتم ، عن اكلها يوم السبت

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r3.speaker: طائفة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r3.claim: A different group held that the Sabbath ban covered eating, frightening the fish away, and catching them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r3.anchor: وقالت طائفة بل نهيتم ، عن اكلها وتنفيرها وصيدها في يوم السبت

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes three factions: the fish offenders, people who warned them, and a group that withdrew and remained silent.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r4.anchor: قعدت الطائفة بانفسها ونسائها وابناءها واعتزلت طائفة ذات اليمين ونهت واعتزلت طائفة ذات الشمال وسكتت

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the admonishers' excuse as expressing their disapproval of the offenders' deeds, while hoping the offenders would fear God.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم في سخطنا اعمالهم ولعلهم يتقون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the warners saying God forbids the conduct and warning offenders not to incur His punishment; when they persisted, the warners condemned them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1600/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس قال : الا يمنون ويلكم الله الله ويلكم ينهاكم الله لا تعرضوا لعقوبة الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1601/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1601/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1601/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd explains the hope that the offenders would stop the conduct they were continuing.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1601/r1.anchor: لعلهم يتقون لعلهم يتركون هذا الفعل الذي هم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r3.claim: This إذ-clause coordinates with the earlier إذ يعدون; it means “ask them about the time a group said,” with إذ a past-time noun rather than an adverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r3.anchor: جملة : { وإذ قالت أمة منهم } عطف على قوله : { إذ يعدون } ( الأعراف : 163 ) والتقدير : واسأل بني إسرائيل إذ قالت أمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r4.claim: The pronoun refers back to the people whom the Prophet is told to ask, not to the town, since the passage rebukes all the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r4.anchor: والضمير المجرور بمن عائد إلى ما عاد إليه ضمير { أسألهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r5.claim: Even if the dialogue occurred in that town, its location is incidental: the story displays another instance of Israelite defiance and the poor effect of admonition, known among their scholars and righteous people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r5.anchor: بل منظورا إليه بأنه مظهر آخر من مظاهر عصيانهم وعتوهم وقلة جدوى الموعظة فيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r6.claim: Here umma means a group sharing this statement; commentators describe three groups: persistent admonishers, admonishers who despaired, and people persisting in wrongdoing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p150/r6.anchor: والأمة الجماعة من الناس المشتركة في هذا القول ، قال المفسرون : إن أمة من بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r1.claim: The verse abbreviates the groups’ prior history: the question shows they had objected after seeing admonition fail, while 7:165 identifies the warners as the rescued group and the wrongdoers as the punished group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r1.anchor: وقد أجملت الآية ما كان من الأمة القائلة إيجازا في الكلام ، اعتمادا على القرينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur connects the term for admonition to its earlier uses at 4:63 and 7:145.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر الوعظ عند قوله تعالى : { فأعرض عنهم وعظهم في سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r3.claim: The لام asks for a reason; the question is censuring and effectively denies any reason to admonish when the addressees believe no one can be brought to heed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r3.anchor: واللام في لم تعظون } للتعليم ، فالمستفهم عنه من نوع العلل ، والاستفهام إنكاري في معنى النفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r4.claim: The people addressed by تعظون are a different group from the group asking why they admonish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r5.claim: The active participles refer to the future; their alternative wording shows that one of two punishments is certain, while which one remains undetermined.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r5.anchor: واسما الفاعل في قوله : { مهلكهم أو معذبهم } مستعملان في معنى الاستقبال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r6.claim: The answer is set off as a separate sentence because it occurs within a dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r6.anchor: وفصلت جملة { قالوا } لوقوعها في سياق المحاورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r7.claim: معذرة is an irregular mimetic verbal noun from اعتذر, meaning to present an excuse; an excuse is a reason or proof offered to remove blame, and اعتذار takes إلى in the sense of conveying it to someone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p151/r7.anchor: والمعذرة بفتح الميم وكسر الذال مصدر ميمي لفعل ( اعتذر ) على غير قياس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r1.speaker: الجمهور وحفص عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r1.claim: Most readers read معذرة in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject (“our admonition is an excuse”); Hafs from Asim reads it accusative of purpose (“we admonish to excuse ourselves”).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r1.anchor: وبالرفع قرأه الجمهور ، وقرأه حفص عن عاصم بالنصب على المفعول لأجله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r2.claim: Hope that they may become God-fearing is a second reason to persist in admonition, since repetition may affect them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r2.anchor: وقوله : { ولعلهم يتقون } علة ثانية للاستمرار على الموعظة أي رجاء لتأثير الموعظة فيهم بتكرارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r3.claim: One righteous group despaired of admonition and expected punishment; another still hoped repetition might work, so it continued to preach as a precaution and excuse before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p152/r3.anchor: فالفريق الأول أخذوا بالطرف الراجح الموجب للظن . والفريق الثاني أخذوا بالطرف المرجوح جمعا بينه وبين الراجح لقصد الاحتياط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r1.claim: Most commentators say the Israelites divided into three groups: Sabbath fishers, public opponents who admonished and withdrew, and a third group that neither sinned nor forbade.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المفسرين: إن بني إسرائيل افترقت ثلاث فرق، فرقة عصت وصادت، وفرقة نهت وجاهرت وتكلمت واعتزلت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r2.claim: The uninvolved group asked why the admonishers warned people God would destroy or severely punish, judging from likelihood and God's prior treatment of sinful nations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r2.anchor: قالت للناهية لم تعظون قوما يريدون العاصية الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم على غلبة الظن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r3.speaker: الناهون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r3.claim: The admonishers answer that their warning is an excuse before their Lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r3.anchor: فقالت الناهية موعظتنا معذرة إلى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r6.speaker: ابن الكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r6.claim: Ibn al-Kalbi, as transmitted by al-Tabari, says there were only two groups: open sinners and people who forbade, opposed, and withdrew; the sinners mocked the admonishers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الكلبي فيما أسند عنه الطبري إن بني إسرائيل لم تفترق إلا فرقتين، فرقة عصت وجاهرت وفرقة نهت وغيرت واعتزلت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the three-group account because 'to your Lord' and 'perhaps they' presuppose distinct addressees and a third party.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r7.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والقول الأول أصوب، وتؤيده الضمائر في قوله: إلى ربكم ولعلهم فهذه المخاطبة تقتضي مخاطبا ومخاطبا ومكنيا عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r8.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r8.claim: These readers pronounce maʿdhira nominative, construing it as 'our admonition is an excuse,' an establishment of their excuse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «معذرة» بالرفع، أي موعظتنا، معذرة أي إقامة عذر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r9.speaker: عاصم وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r9.claim: Asim in some transmissions, Isa ibn Umar, and Talha ibn Musarrif read maʿdhira in the accusative, meaning that their admonishing is an excuse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r9.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في بعض ما روي عنه وعيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف «معذرة» بالنصب أي وعظنا معذرة، قال أبو علي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r10.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r10.claim: Abu Ali cites Sibawayh's rule that someone saying 'an excuse to God and you' would use the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي حجتها أن سيبويه قال: لو قال رجل لرجل معذرة إلى الله وإليك من كذا لنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya distinguishes that example from the verse: the hypothetical speaker apologizes for himself, unlike the Israelite admonishers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r11.anchor: الرجل القائل في هذا المثال معتذر عن نفسه وليس كذلك الناهون من بني إسرائيل فتأمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r12.claim: The threatened destruction would occur in this world, while the alternative severe punishment would be in the Hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r12.anchor: ومعنى مهلكهم في الدنيا أو معذبهم في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r13.claim: Laʿallahum yattaqūn expresses unqualified hope because the phrase is spoken by human beings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p468/r13.anchor: وقوله: لعلهم يتقون يقتضي الترجي المحض، لأنه من قول آدميين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r1.claim: Exegetes describe three village factions: one fished and ate the catch, one forbade and rebuked them, and one refrained from fishing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون افترق أهل القرية ثلاث فرق فرقة صادت وأكلت وفرقة نهت وزجرت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r2.claim: The non-fishing faction reproached the preachers for admonishing people they believed would not stop, since God would destroy or severely punish them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r2.anchor: لاموهم على موعظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين فقالت الفرقة الناهية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r3.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r3.claim: These readers pronounce maʿdhira in the nominative; the preaching itself is an excuse before God, since enjoining right is obligatory.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي معذرة رفعا أي موعظتنا إياهم معذرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r4.claim: Hafs transmits from ʿAsim the accusative reading maʿdhiratan, meaning that the speakers offer an excuse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r4.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم معذرة نصبا وذلك على معنى نعتذر معذرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r5.claim: The admonishers say that warning the sinners excuses them before God because they must enjoin what is right.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r5.anchor: والمعنى أن الأمر بالمعروف واجب علينا فعلينا موعظة هؤلاء عذرا إلى الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r6.claim: It remains possible that the warning will benefit them and lead them to abandon the sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p277/r6.anchor: أي وجائز أن ينتفعوا بالموعظة فيتركوا المعصية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir divides the village into Sabbath fishers, people who forbade them and withdrew, and a silent group that neither sinned nor forbade.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r1.anchor: صاروا إلى ثلاث فرق: فرقة (1) ارتكبت المحذور، واحتالوا على اصطياد السمك يوم السبت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r2.claim: The silent faction asked why admonish people already doomed to destruction or severe punishment, since warning them seemed useless.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r2.anchor: وقد علمتم أنهم هلكوا واستحقوا العقوبة من الله؟ فلا فائدة في نهيكم إياهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r3.claim: The admonishers said they warned to discharge before God their duty to command right and forbid wrong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r3.anchor: فيما أخذ علينا من الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r4.claim: They hoped their rebuke would make the sinners desist, fear God, repent, and receive His mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r4.anchor: يتقون ما هم فيه ويتركونه، ويرجعون إلى الله تائبين، فإذا تابوا تاب الله عليهم ورحمهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r5.speaker: قرّاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r5.claim: Some readers put maʿdhira in the nominative, understood as this is an excuse; others put it in the accusative, meaning they act as an excuse before God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r5.anchor: قرأ بعضهم بالرفع، كأنه على تقديره: هذا معذرة وقرأ آخرون بالنصب، أي: نفعل ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, locates the village at Aylah between Egypt and Medina: fish appeared openly on the Sabbath and disappeared afterward; some Israelites caught them despite prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r9.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s account, both groups of admonishers, including those who questioned further warnings, were saved; God turned the fish catchers into apes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494/r9.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.claim: Al-Awfi also transmits from Ibn Abbas an account close to the preceding report about the Sabbath village.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.anchor: وروى العوفي، عن ابن عباس قريبا من هذا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas first said he did not know whether the questioners survived; after the narrator pressed him, he affirmed they did and gave him a cloak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} قال: ما أدري أنجا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.claim: Ikrima recounts Ibn Abbas’s detailed Aylah story: Satan suggested taking Sabbath fish and eating them later, while another group held that catching them was also forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا ابن جريج، حدثني رجل، عن عكرمة قال: جئت ابن عباس يوما وهو يبكي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.claim: In Ikrima’s report, the active admonishers said they warned as an excuse before God and hoped the offenders would stop; they then separated themselves from the sinners.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.anchor: قال الأيمنون: {معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون} إن ينتهوا فهو أحب إلينا ألا يصابوا ولا يهلكوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas’s report through Ibn Ishaq and Ikrima describes a man tying a fish on the Sabbath and openly eating it later while most people failed to object.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق، عن داود بن الحصين، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس؛ أنه قال: ابتدعوا السبت فابتلوا فيه، فحرمت عليهم فيه الحيتان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r2.claim: In this account Ibn Abbas divides them into thirds: warners, questioners who asked why admonish, and sinners; only the warners survived.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا أثلاثا: ثلث نهوا، وثلث قالوا: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r3.claim: Mujahid also transmitted the Ibn Abbas account of the Sabbath people.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r4.speaker: ابن رومان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r4.claim: Ibn Ruman reports that a man tethered Sabbath fish until Sunday, then taught others the loophole; the practice spread and the city was struck by transformation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r4.anchor: عن مالك، قال: زعم ابن رومان أن قوله تعالى: {تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says he had already presented sufficient reports about this village in his commentary on al-Baqara.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p495/r6.anchor: من الآثار في خبر هذه القرية ما فيه مقنع وكفاية،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p496/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p496/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p496/r1.claim: Although the alternative report has a good chain, Ibn Kathir prefers Ibn Abbas’s return to Ikrima’s view that the silent questioners survived, since their later status became clear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p496/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد جيد عن ابن عباس، ولكن رجوعه إلى قول عكرمة في نجاة الساكتين، أولى من القول بهذا؛

JISHUMI:v4p2753/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative, as an implied 'we do this as an excuse' or 'we excuse ourselves.'
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r2.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم معذرة بالنصب أي نفعل ذلك معذرة أو نعتذر معذرة

JISHUMI:v4p2753/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r3.speaker: باقي القراء
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r3.claim: The other readers use the nominative, understood as 'this is an excuse' or 'our statement is an excuse,' with an omitted subject.
JISHUMI:v4p2753/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالرفع؛ أي: هذه معذرة، أو قولنا معذرة، فهي خبر ابتداء محذوف

MUQATIL:7:164-166/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r1.claim: The group questioning the admonition was a band of wrongdoers addressing those who warned about Sabbath fishing.
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r1.anchor: { وإذا قالت أمة منهم } ، يعني عصابة منهم، وهى الظلمة للواعظة،

MUQATIL:7:164-166/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r2.claim: The admonishers had warned the fishers about the fish and threatened punishment, but the wrongdoers did not heed them.
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r2.anchor: وذلك أن الواعظة نهوهم عن الحيتان، وخوفوهم فلم ينتبهوا،

MUQATIL:7:164-166/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r3.claim: The admonishers acted to have an excuse before God and so that the offenders might desist, have punishment deferred, or be saved.
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r3.anchor: { قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم } ، يعني ولكى ينتهوا فيؤخروا أو يعذبوا فينجوا،

MUQATIL:7:164-166/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:164-166/r4.claim: Laʿallahum yattaqūn means “so that they may avoid sins.”

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r1.claim: The opening is coordinated with the earlier إذ يعدون, with the same syntactic treatment.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r1.anchor: معطوف على إذ يعدون وحمه كحمه فى الإعراب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r2.claim: The group is the village's righteous people, who had lost hope after exhorters tried every approach and others persisted in sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r2.anchor: تجماعة من صلحاء القرية الذين أيسوا من وعظهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r3.claim: They ask because they think preaching cannot benefit people whom God will destroy or punish.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r3.anchor: و إنما قاوال ذلك لعلهم أن الوعظ لا ينفع فيهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r4.claim: The preachers say they admonish to establish their excuse before God, so they are not blamed for neglecting to forbid wrong.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r4.anchor: أى موعظتنا إبلاء عذر إلى الله لئلا ننسب فى النهى عن المنكر إلى التفريط

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r5.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative as an object of purpose: they preached to make an excuse.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r5.anchor: معذرة حفص على أنه مفعول له أى وعظناهم للمعذرة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p43#2/r6.claim: They also hope that the admonished people will become mindful.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#2/r11.claim: On the two-group account, the sinners ask the admonishers why they warn them if God will destroy or severely punish them; God then transforms them into apes.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#2/r11.anchor: فعلى هذا القول إن بني إسرائيل لم تفترق إلا فرقتين. ويكون المعنى في قوله تعالى: { وإذا قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r1.claim: The admonishing group says warning is an excuse before God and is offered in hope that the sinners will become God-fearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r1.anchor: فقالت الناهية: موعظتنا معذرة إلى الله لعلهم يتقون.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r2.claim: The wording supports three groups: with only two, the warners would have addressed sinners directly with laʿallakum tattaqun, using the second-person suffix.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r2.anchor: ولو كانوا فرقتين لقالت الناهية للعاصية: ولعلكم تتقون، بالكاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r3.claim: One view says the third group, which neither sinned nor warned, perished with the sinners as punishment for abandoning the duty to warn; Ibn Abbas also says he did not know their fate, which al-Qurtubi calls the apparent reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r3.anchor: قاله ابن عباس. وقال أيضا: ما أدري ما فعل بهم وهو الظاهر من الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r4.claim: Ikrima argued to Ibn Abbas that the third group disliked the sinners' conduct and separated from them; he eventually persuaded Ibn Abbas that they survived, and Ibn Abbas gave him a robe. Al-Hasan shares this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: قلت لابن عباس لما قال ما أدري ما فعل بهم: ألا ترى أنهم قد كرهوا ما هم عليه وخالفوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites the destruction of the wrongdoers alone as evidence that only the Sabbath transgressors perished, invoking al-Araf and al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r5.anchor: ومما يدل على أنه إنما هلكت الفرقة العادية لا غير قوله: «وأخذنا الذين ظلموا».

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r6.speaker: عيسى وطلحة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r6.claim: Isa and Talha read maʿdhiratan in the accusative; al-Kisai gives a verbal-noun reading or an implied meaning, we did this as an excuse. Hafs is also cited for the accusative, while the rest read nominative.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وطلحة «معذرة» بالنصب. ونصبه عند الكسائي من وجهين: أحدهما على المصدر. والثاني على تقدير فعلنا ذلك معذرة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r7.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the nominative because they describe their warning as an excuse in answer to a question, rather than initiating a new apology; an explicit apology from one person to another would be accusative, according to Sibawayh.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r7.anchor: والباقون بالرفع: وهو الاختيار لأنهم لم يريدوا أن يعتذروا اعتذارا مستأنفا من أمر ليموا عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the verse supports the legal principle of blocking the means, discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r8.anchor: ودلت الآية على القول بسد الذرائع. وقد مضى في «البقرة».

QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r9.claim: The discussion cross-refers to al-Baqara on whether transformed people reproduce, Ali Imran and al-Maida on enjoining right and forbidding wrong, and al-Nisa on avoiding corrupt company.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:163-164#3/r9.anchor: ومضى في «آل عمران» و«المائدة» الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر.

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.claim: Wa-idh qālat is coordinated with idh yaʿdūn and has the same grammatical parsing.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن قوله : { وإذ قالت } معطوف على قوله : { إذ يعدون } وحكمه حكمه في الإعراب

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r2.claim: The group is a righteous faction from the town that exerted every effort advising the fishers.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r2.anchor: وقوله : { أمة منهم } أي جماعة من أهل القرية من صلحائهم الذين ركبوا الصعب والذلول في موعظة أولئك الصيادين

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r3.claim: The questioners think admonition pointless because the offenders persist in evil and are unlikely to heed it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r3.anchor: وإنما قالوا ذلك لعلمهم أن الوعظ لا ينفعهم وقوله : { قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم }

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r4.claim: Muhl ikuhum means removing them and cleansing the earth of them; the alternative is severe punishment for their persistence in evil.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r4.anchor: أي مخترمهم ومطهر الأرض منهم { أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا } لتماديهم في الشر

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r5.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative; the other readers read it nominative.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r5.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم { معذرة } بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses the accusative as an implied verb meaning they offer an excuse; the nominative supplies an omitted subject such as this is an excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r6.anchor: أما من نصب { معذرة } فقال الزجاج معناه : نعتذر معذرة ، وأما من رفع فالتقدير : هذه معذرة

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r7.claim: Abū Zayd explains ʿudhr and maʿdhira as standing up for someone's excuse; the admonishers excuse themselves before God by having warned.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو زيد : عذرته أعذره عذرا ومعذرة ، ومعنى عذره في اللغة أي قام بعذره

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r8.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r8.claim: Al-Azharī says maʿdhira is a noun on the mafʿila pattern used instead of iʿtidhār, as though preaching were an apology to God.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r8.anchor: وقال الأزهري : المعذرة اسم على مفعلة من عذر يعذر وأقيم مقام الاعتذار .

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r9.claim: Their excuse means they fulfilled their duty to God by continuing to forbid wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r9.anchor: فعلى هذا معنى قوله : { معذرة إلى ربكم } أي قيام منا بعذر أنفسنا إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r10.claim: They consider it possible their advice may benefit the offenders, leading them to fear God and stop sinning.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r10.anchor: أي وجائز عندنا أن ينتفعوا بهذا الوعظ فيتقوا الله ويتركوا هذا الذنب

RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r11.claim: One account divides the townspeople into offenders, admonishers, and a silent faction that rebukes admonition as pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v15p32#2/r11.anchor: أن أهل القرية منهم من صاد السمك وأقدم على ذلك الذنب ومنهم من لم يفعل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the three-faction account: if admonishers addressed sinners, they would say perhaps you will fear God, not perhaps they will.
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : والقول الأول أصح ، لأنهم لو كانوا فرقتين وكان قوله : { معذرة إلى ربكم } خطابا

RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r2.claim: A second account has two factions: offenders who challenge the admonishers, and those who refrain from sin and warn them.
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن أهل القرية كانوا فرقتين : فرقة أقدمت على الذنب ، وفرقة أحجموا عنه ووعظوا الأولين

RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have suspended judgment about which faction asked why the offenders were admonished.
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r5.anchor: فنقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه توقف فيه .

RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r6.claim: Another report says sinners and silent critics perished while admonishers survived; Ibn ʿAbbās wept and warned that those silent about wrong also perish.
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r6.anchor: ونقل عنه أيضا : هلكت الفرقتان ونجت الناهية ، وكان ابن عباس إذا قرأ هذه الآية بكى

RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the silent faction survived, so two factions were saved; critics stopped advising because they expected no benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v15p33/r7.anchor: قال الحسن : الفرقة الساكتة ناجية ، فعلى هذا نجت فرقتان وهلكت الثالثة .

STUDYQURAN:7:164/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r1.claim: The community comprises Israelites who neither fished on the Sabbath nor admonished those who did.
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r1.anchor: those Israelites in the town who did not participate in fishing on the Sabbath, but also did not admonish those who did

STUDYQURAN:7:164/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r2.speaker: community
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r2.claim: Those who did not admonish ask the active admonishers why they warn people God is about to destroy or severely punish.
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r2.anchor: asking why they make the effort to admonish a people whom God is about to destroy or punish

STUDYQURAN:7:164/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r3.speaker: admonishers
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r3.claim: The admonishers say they act as an excuse before God because forbidding wrong is an obligation and doing so fulfills their moral duty.
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r3.anchor: they consider themselves to be obligated to “forbid wrong,” and having done so, they have fulfilled their moral duty

STUDYQURAN:7:164/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r4.speaker: admonishers
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r4.claim: They also hope their warning will bring Sabbath violators back to reverence for God and Mosaic Law.
STUDYQURAN:7:164/r4.anchor: hoped that their warnings might succeed in bringing the Sabbath violators back to reverence for God and for Mosaic Law

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to recall a group asking why others admonish Sabbath violators whom God will destroy in this world for disobedience or punish severely in the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r1.anchor: السبت وتنهاهم عن معصية الله فيه: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] في الدنيا بمعصيتهم إياه

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r2.claim: The admonishers answer that they warn the violators to discharge their duty before God by enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r2.anchor: مجيبيهم عن قولهم: عظتنا إياهم {معذرة إلى ربكم} [الأعراف: 164] نؤدي فرضه علينا في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r3.claim: They hope the violators will fear God, return to obedience, repent, and stop transgressing the Sabbath prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r3.anchor: ولعلهم أن يتقوا الله فيخافوه، فينيبوا إلى طاعته ويتوبوا من معصيتهم إياه

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses their excuse as disapproval of the offenders' deeds and their hope as that the offenders desist.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم} [الأعراف: 164] لسخطنا أعمالهم. {ولعلهم يتقون} [الأعراف: 164] أي: ينزعون عما هم عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd explains the hope as that they abandon the practice they are committing.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {ولعلهم يتقون} [الأعراف: 164] قال: يتركون هذا العمل الذي هم عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r6.speaker: عامة قراء الحجاز والكوفة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r6.claim: Most readers in the Hijaz, Kufa, and Basra read maʿdhira in the nominative, as the excuse described in the explanation.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r6.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء الحجاز والكوفة والبصرة: (معذرة) بالرفع على ما وصفت من معناها

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r7.speaker: بعض أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r7.claim: Some Kufan readers read maʿdhira in the accusative, meaning an act of apologizing: they admonished and did so as an excuse.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r7.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض أهل الكوفة: {معذرة} [الأعراف: 164] نصبا، بمعنى: إعذارا وعظناهم وفعلنا ذلك

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r8.claim: One reported view holds that the group asking why admonish was among the saved, since it too belonged to those forbidding the Sabbath violation.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r8.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كانت من الناجية؛ لأنها كانت من الناهية الفرقة الهالكة عن الاعتداء في السبت

TAB-FULL:v10p511/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas locates the story at Aylah: after fish came only on the Sabbath, two groups admonished the violators; both groups were saved and the fish-takers became apes and swine.
TAB-FULL:v10p511/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} [الأعراف: 164] هي قرية على شاطئ البحر

TAB-FULL:v10p516/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers warned Sabbath fish-takers; some judged them doomed, while the admonishers hoped either to be spared or to earn reward if the offenders repented.
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {واسألهم عن القرية التي، كانت حاضرة البحر} [الأعراف: 163] إلى قوله: {ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم}

TAB-FULL:v10p516/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Israelites shifted their assigned worship day from Monday to Saturday, after which Moses forbade work on the Sabbath; a woodcutter was seized and stoned by his companions.
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r2.anchor: وقد كان الله جعل على بني إسرائيل يوما يعبدونه ويتفرغون له فيه، وهو يوم الاثنين، فتعدى الخبثاء من الاثنين إلى السبت

TAB-FULL:v10p516/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says one group questioned admonishing people who had already ignored warnings, while the admonishers replied that it was an excuse before God and perhaps the people would become cautious.
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " قال بعض الذين نهوهم لبعض: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا}

TAB-FULL:v10p516/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas initially said he did not know whether the questioners were saved; Ikrima kept pressing him until he acknowledged they had been saved, then Ibn Abbas gave him a cloak.
TAB-FULL:v10p516/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: " {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} [الأعراف: 164] قال: ما أدري أنجا

TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas wept because the third faction was not mentioned and feared his community might resemble them; Ikrima reassured him by pointing to God's statement that the transgressors exceeded their prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: دخلت على ابن عباس والمصحف في حجره وهو يبكي، فقلت: ما يبكيك جعلني الله فداءك

TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r2.claim: In Ikrima's account, Ibn Abbas recounts that Satan persuaded some Jews to catch Sabbath fish for later eating; one group violated, one warned, and a silent group questioned the warnings. The warners separated, the offenders became apes, and the animals acknowledged the warning; Ibn Abbas says only the warners are explicitly saved.
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: جئت ابن عباس يوما وهو يبكي، وإذا المصحف في حجره

TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warnings are named among the saved but cannot see the fate of the others, and fears that people who see wrongdoing yet stay silent may share the third faction's fate.
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا أسمع الفرقة الثالثة ذكرت نخاف أن نكون مثلهم

TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r4.claim: Ikrima argues that the questioners opposed the wrongdoing and dissented from the offenders, so they should be counted among those who resisted; Ibn Abbas accepts the point and has him clothed.
TAB-FULL:v10p516#2/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: جئت ابن عباس يوما وهو يبكي، وإذا المصحف في حجره

TAB-FULL:v10p517/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r1.claim: Qatada divides the people into three groups: those who refrained and forbade the sin, those who refrained out of reverence for God, and those who violated the prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " {واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر} [الأعراف: 163] ذكر لنا أنه إذا كان يوم السبت

TAB-FULL:v10p517/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas's report says the sole faction exempt from the punishment did not violate the Sabbath and warned the violators; some members of this faction asked why admonish them.
TAB-FULL:v10p517/r3.anchor: إلا طائفة منهم لم يعتدوا ونهوهم، فقال بعضهم لبعض: {لم تعظون قوما}

TAB-FULL:v10p518/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the hope that they may become cautious as hope that they will leave their current practice.
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] حتى بلغ: {ولعلهم يتقون} [الأعراف: 164] لعلهم يتركون ما هم عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p518/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts a fish-taking loophole that spread after a man tethered fish and pulled them out after the Sabbath; two admonishing groups then differed, but God saved all who warned while punishing those who persisted.
TAB-FULL:v10p518/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] حتى بلغ

TAB-FULL:v10p519/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas first said he did not know whether the questioners survived, then acknowledged they were saved after Ikrima continued pressing him; he gave Ikrima a cloak.
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: قرأ ابن عباس هذه الآية: " {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} [الأعراف: 164] قال: لا أدري أنجا القوم
