TAB-FULL:v10p519/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r2.speaker: ابن رومان
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r2.claim: Ibn Ruman recounts that a man tied Sabbath fish in the water, concealed the catch, and taught the practice to others; the town was enclosed, its people became apes, and the transformed apes approached their former neighbors.
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r2.anchor: عن مالك، قال: زعم ابن رومان أن قوله: {تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم} [الأعراف: 163] قال: كانت تأتيهم يوم السبت

TAB-FULL:v10p519/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r3.claim: Another reported view says the faction that asked why admonish was itself among the doomed factions.
TAB-FULL:v10p519/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل الفرقة التي قالت: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] كانت من الفرقة الهالكة

TAB-FULL:v10p521/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas divides the people into thirds: warners, those who questioned warning, and offenders; only the warners survived, while the others perished and were transformed into apes, as a warning linked to the earlier Sabbath punishment.
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا أثلاثا: ثلث نهوا، وثلث قالوا: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164]

TAB-FULL:v10p521/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r2.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says the warners survived and the offenders perished, but he does not know what happened to those who remained silent.
TAB-FULL:v10p521/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء} [الأعراف: 165] الآية، قال ابن عباس: نجا الناهون، وهلك الفاعلون، ولا أدري ما صنع بالساكتين

TAB-FULL:v10p522/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Qatada, identifies three factions but leaves the fate of the third—the people asking why admonish—unknown.
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن ابن عباس: " {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] قال: هم ثلاث فرق

TAB-FULL:v10p522/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r2.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says there were only two factions: the admonishers and those who asked why, who were the people being admonished.
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هما فرقتان: الفرقة التي وعظت، والفرقة التي قالت: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] قال: هي الموعوظة

TAB-FULL:v10p522/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says he would prefer to know the fate of those who asked why admonish over any other piece of knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: " لأن أكون علمت من هؤلاء الذين قالوا: {لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} [الأعراف: 164] أحب إلي

TAB-FULL:v10p522/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas cites God's saving the warners and punishing the wrongdoers, then wonders aloud what became of the questioners.
TAB-FULL:v10p522/r4.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم} [الأعراف: 164] قال: أسمع الله يقول: {أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس}

TABATABAI:7:161-165/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r1.claim: These episodes recount earlier Israelites breaking God's commands and covenant and being punished; later generations inherited their scripture but traded its signs cheaply and relaxed religious observance, with only a few remaining true.
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r1.anchor: بيان قصص أخرى من قصص بني إسرائيل فسقوا فيها عن أمر الله

TABATABAI:7:161-165/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r8.claim: The question came from one group to another that admonished the Sabbath violators; the questioners were pious in other respects but had stopped forbidding wrong and continued associating with the violators.
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r8.anchor: إنما قالت هذه الأمة ما قالت، لامة أخرى منهم كانت تعظهم

TABATABAI:7:161-165/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r9.claim: Although the offenders were openly defiant and a plain warning might not stop them, the admonishers kept hoping that some would heed, and at minimum sought to show God they did not approve the sin.
TABATABAI:7:161-165/r9.anchor: وكانوا يرجون منهم الانتهاء لو استمروا في عظتهم

TABATABAI:7:164-166/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:164-166/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:164-166/r1.claim: They admonish to have an excuse before God and because they hope the people may become God-fearing; saying your Lord rather than our Lord signals that the duty belongs to the questioners too.
TABATABAI:7:164-166/r1.anchor: وفي قولهم { إلى ربكم } حيث أضافوا الرب إلى اللائمين ولم يقولوا إلى ربنا إشارة إلى أن التكليف بالعظة ليس مختصا بنا

TABATABAI:7:170-171/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:170-171/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:170-171/r5.claim: Al-Bāqir, citing ʿAlī's book, says Sabbath fish were sent visibly; some exploited a loophole to catch them that day and eat later, while one faction warned and withdrew, another stayed silent, and the warners ultimately left town fearing shared punishment.
TABATABAI:7:170-171/r5.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال وجدنا في كتاب علي عليه السلام أن قوما من أهل إيلة من قوم ثمود

TABRISI:7:163-164/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ reads maʿdhiratan with accusative; the other readers use nominative.
TABRISI:7:163-164/r1.anchor: القراءة: قرأ حفص معذرة بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

TABRISI:7:163-164/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164/r2.claim: Nominative means “our admonition is an excuse,” with an omitted subject; accusative means “we apologize.” Sibawayh gives the same accusative construction.
TABRISI:7:163-164/r2.anchor: من قرأ معذرة بالرفع فتقديره موعظتنا معذرة فيكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

TABRISI:7:163-164/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164/r9.claim: Maʿdhira and related ʿudhr terms name an excuse; al-muʿdhir has a valid excuse, while al-muʿadhdhir pretends to have one and is negligent.
TABRISI:7:163-164/r9.anchor: والمعذرة والعذر والعذرى والعذرة واحد مصدر عذرته أعذره

TABRISI:7:163-164/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164/r10.claim: Muʿtadhir can describe someone with or without an excuse; man yaʿdhurunī asks who will uphold his excuse.
TABRISI:7:163-164/r10.anchor: والمعتذر يقال لمن له عذر ولمن لا عذر له وقولهم من يعذرني

TABRISI:7:163-164/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164/r14.claim: Lam taʿiẓūn is originally limā; the alif drops after a preposition, as in mim, fīm, ʿalām, and ʿam.
TABRISI:7:163-164/r14.anchor: أصله لما ولكن هذه الألف تحذف مع حرف الجر

TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r6.claim: The people divided into fishers, silent observers, and admonishers; the silent group addressed the admonishers.
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r6.anchor: وكانوا ثلاث فرق فرقة قانصة وفرقة ساكتة وفرقة واعظة

TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r7.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r7.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the silent group asked from despair that sinners would accept admonition; commanding right is obligatory only while acceptance is not hopeless.

TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r8.claim: They expected God to destroy the people in this world for disobedience or punish them severely in the afterlife.

TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r9.claim: The admonishers say their warning discharges their duty to God in forbidding wrongdoing, so God cannot ask why they failed to warn.
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r9.anchor: معناه موعظتنا إياهم معذرة إلى الله وتأدية لفرضه في النهي عن المنكر

TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:163-164#2/r10.claim: They also admonish in hope that the people will become God-fearing and return.

FARRA:v1p397/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p397/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p397/r11.claim: The speakers mean that they admonished the people as an excuse before their Lord.

FARRA:v1p397/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p397/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p397/r12.claim: Although Arabs usually put معذرة in the accusative, al-Farrāʾ prefers the readers’ nominative; the accusative is also valid.
FARRA:v1p397/r12.anchor: وقد آثرت القراء رفعها. ونصبها جائز

FARRA:v1p397/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p397/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p397/r13.claim: On the nominative reading, معذرة is a predicate, as in إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ.
FARRA:v1p397/r13.anchor: فمن رفع قال: هي معذرة كما قال: إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ.

THALABI:v4p296/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p296/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v4p296/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the groups were separated by a wall; after David cursed the wrongdoers, the admonishers found them transformed into monkeys, recognized their kin, and the monkeys wept and nodded that they had been warned.
THALABI:v4p296/r6.anchor: فقسموا القرية بجدار للمسلمين باب وللمعتدين باب ولعنهم داود (عليه السلام) فأصبح الناهون ذات يوم

THALABI:v4p297/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p297/r2.claim: Scholars disagreed whether the group asking why the sinners were admonished belonged to the saved or the doomed.
THALABI:v4p297/r2.anchor: واختلف العلماء في الفرقة الذين قالوا: (لم تعظون قوما) كانت من الناجية أو من الهالكة؟

THALABI:v4p297/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r3.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p297/r3.claim: One view says they were saved because they themselves belonged to the group that forbade wrongdoing.
THALABI:v4p297/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كانت من الناجية لأنها كانت من الناهية.

THALABI:v4p297/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r4.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v4p297/r4.claim: The opposing view says they were among the transgressors: they had warned the sinners that punishment was certain, then questioned the point of admonishing them.
THALABI:v4p297/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: كانت من الفرقة الهالكة، لأنهم كانوا من الخاطئة

THALABI:v4p297/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r5.speaker: حفص
THALABI:v4p297/r5.claim: Hafs reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative, meaning they admonished as an excuse before their Lord.
THALABI:v4p297/r5.anchor: وقرأ حفص: معذرة أي يفعل ذلك معذرة ولعلهم يتقون صيد الحيتان

THALABI:v4p297/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p297/r6.claim: Thaʿlabi concludes the questioners were among the saved and believers addressed one another; if they addressed the sinners, they would say ‘perhaps you will be wary.’
THALABI:v4p297/r6.anchor: والصواب أنها كانت من الفرقة الناجية وأن هذا الكلام من قول المؤمنين بعضهم لبعض لأنه لو كان الخطاب للمعتدين

THALABI:v4p297/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r7.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
THALABI:v4p297/r7.claim: Yaman ibn Riʾab supports the saved reading, saying the two statements belonged to groups that were spared while fish catchers were punished.
THALABI:v4p297/r7.anchor: يدل عليه قول يمان بن رئاب نحن الطائفتان اللذان قالوا لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم

THALABI:v4p297/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p297/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p297/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas wished he knew what happened to the questioners; Ikrima argued they had rejected the sinners’ behavior, and Ibn Abbas was persuaded and gave him a robe.
THALABI:v4p297/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ليت شعري ما فعل هؤلاء الذين قالوا: لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r1.claim: The commentators divide the town into Sabbath fishers and eaters, a group that forbade and rebuked them, and a group that refrained from fishing and questioned the admonishers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r1.anchor: افترق أهل القرية ثلاث فرق؛ فرقة صادت وأكلت، وفرقة نهت وزجرت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the quiet group blamed the admonishers because they knew the offenders would not stop; the admonishers replied that enjoining right was their duty and an excuse before God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: (لاموهم على موعظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r3.claim: Maʿdhira is a verbal noun like ʿudhr.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r4.claim: Abu Zayd gives the forms ʿadhartuhu, aʿdhiruhu, ʿudhran, maʿdhiratan, and ʿudhrā for excusing someone.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r5.claim: The root means to stand up for or accept someone's excuse; the admonishers say their warning will let them answer God that they performed their duty and are excused.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى عذره في اللغة (¬4): قام بعذره، وقبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r6.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r6.claim: Al-Azhari calls maʿdhira a noun on the mafʿila pattern standing for an act of apology, as though the speakers said their admonition is an apology to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p412#2/r6.anchor: المعذرة اسم على مفعلة من عذر يعذر، وأقيم مقام الاعتذار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi points to the related expression in 9:66, previously discussed in the chapter on repentance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says ʿudhr, ʿudhrā, and maʿdhira can mean an exit from blame or sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: (يقال: لي في هذا الأمر عذر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r3.claim: Abu Ali says they did not offer a new excuse for an alleged offense; asked why they admonished, they answered that their admonition itself was an excuse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r3.anchor: لم يريدوا أن يعتذروا عذرا مستأنفا من أمر ليموا عليه، ولكنهم قيل لهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r4.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r4.claim: Sibawayh says a speaker would put maʿdhira in the accusative in the construction, I offer an excuse to God and to you regarding such-and-such.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r4.anchor: لو قال رجل لرجل: معذرة إلى الله، وإليك من كذا وكذا لنصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies the omitted verb: the meaning is, we offer an excuse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r6.claim: The admonishers considered it possible that their warning would benefit the offenders, so that they might fear God and stop transgressing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r6.anchor: أي: جائز عندنا أن ينتفعوا بالمعذرة فيتقوا الله ويتركوا العدو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r7.speaker: الكلبي والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r7.claim: A second account has only two groups, the admonishers and the offenders; on this account, those asking why they admonish are the offenders.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r7.anchor: وكانوا فرقتين: فرقة نهت عن السوء، وفرقة عملت بالسوء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says the offenders numbered about seventy thousand and the admonishers about twelve thousand; the offenders asked why they warned if punishment was already known to be near.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r8.anchor: المعتدية نحو من سبعين ألفا أتاهم طوائف نحو من اثني عشر ألفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r9.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers the three-group account: if the admonishers spoke to offenders directly, the pronoun should be laʿallakum, you may fear God, not laʿallahum, they may fear God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p414/r9.anchor: والقول الأول (¬6) أصح؛ لأنهم لو كانوا فرقتين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r4.claim: Those who neither fished nor forbade it asked why admonish people God would destroy, since they knew they would not stop.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r4.anchor: { وإذ قالت أمة منهم } قالوا للفرقة الناهية { لم تعظون قوما الله ملهلكهم } لاموهم على موعظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r5.claim: The admonishers said that commanding right is obligatory and their warning excused them before God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r5.anchor: فقالت الفرقة الناهية للذين لاموهم: { معذرة إلى ربكم } أي: الأمر بالمعروف واجب علينا، فعلينا موعظة هؤلاء عذرا إلى الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r6.claim: They hoped their warning would make offenders fear God and stop fishing on the Sabbath.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:163-165/r6.anchor: { ولعلهم يتقون } فيتركون الصيد في السبت

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r1.claim: Addressed to Jews of the Prophet’s time who already knew the episode, the account is terse; the coastal town apparently also had Sabbath keepers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r1.anchor: Konu hakkında bilgileri bulunan Hz. Peygamber dönemi yahudilerine hitap edildiği için oldukça muhtasar bir üslûp kullanılmakla birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r2.claim: Some warned Sabbath violators; another group thought warning futile because destruction or severe punishment was certain; the admonishers sought to discharge their duty and hoped to help offenders reform.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r2.anchor: diğerleri ise, en azından uyarı görevlerini yapmış sayılmak ve böylece Allah katında sorumluluktan kurtulmak yanında

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r3.claim: The people comprised Sabbath violators, obedient but pessimistic people who saw guidance as useless, and those who considered admonition an inescapable duty and refused despair.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r3.anchor: a) Allah’ın yasaklarını çiğneyenler, b) Allah’ın hükümlerine uymakla birlikte günahkârların ıslah edilmesi konusunda kötümser olup irşadın yararsız olduğunu düşünenler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r4.claim: The verse’s style shows that the third group, who kept admonishing with hope, exemplified the ideal conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r4.anchor: Âyetin üslûbundan, en ideal davranışın bu sonuncularınki olduğu anlaşılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r5.claim: Good believers, especially learned people, should obey God themselves and tirelessly guide others toward the right path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r5.anchor: kendileri Allah’ın buyruk ve yasaklarına uyarak temiz bir hayat yaşadıkları gibi başkalarının da doğru yola gelmelerini sağlamak için bıkıp usanmadan aydınlatma görevlerini yerine getirirler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r6.claim: A genuine educator or guide must not withdraw on the pessimistic assumption that wrongdoing is incurable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r6.anchor: Gerçek bir eğitimci ve irşad edicinin kötümser bir yaklaşımla, kötülükleri çaresiz ve şifasız kabul edip bir kenara çekilmesi doğru bir davranış değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r7.claim: People, including prophets, answer for making the required effort in guidance rather than for their success; guidance itself comes only from God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:164/r7.anchor: insanlar bu hususta ne ölçüde başarılı olduklarından değil, bu yolda gerektiği kadar ve gerektiği şekilde çaba gösterip göstermediklerinden sorumludurlar, hidayet ise yalnız Allah’tandır

BAQILLANI:v1p34/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r2.claim: The Qur'an's third proof of inimitability is its novel composition and extraordinary rhetorical arrangement, which the author says he will explain in detail.
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r2.anchor: والوجه الثالث أنه بديع النظم عجيب التأليف متناه في البلاغة إلى الحد الذي يعلم عجز الخلق عنه

NAHHAS:v2p157/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p157/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p157/r1.claim: The alif is omitted because the word is interrogative; another analysis makes mā a preposition, with hāʾ added at pause to show its vowel.
NAHHAS:v2p157/r1.anchor: الأصل لما حذفت الألف لأنه استفهام وقيل ما حرف خفض فإذا أوقفت في غير القرآن قلت لمه

NAHHAS:v2p157/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p157/r2.speaker: عيسى وطلحة
NAHHAS:v2p157/r2.claim: ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read maʿdhiratan in the accusative.
NAHHAS:v2p157/r2.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وطلحة ( معذرة ) بالنصب ونصبه عند الكسائي من جهتين

NAHHAS:v2p157/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p157/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p157/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows the accusative as a verbal noun or with an implied faʿalnā dhālika maʿdhiratan.
NAHHAS:v2p157/r3.anchor: ونصبه عند الكسائي من جهتين إحداهما أنه مصدر والأخرى أن التقدير فعلنا ذلك معذرة

NAHHAS:v2p157/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p157/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p157/r4.claim: Sībawayh prefers nominative: they answer that admonishing is their excuse to God, not that they are starting a fresh apology for some regretted act. A direct apology to someone would be accusative.
NAHHAS:v2p157/r4.anchor: فقال لأنهم لم يريدوا أن يعتذروا اعتذارا مستأنفا من أمر ليمسوا عليه ولكنهم قيل لهم

TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r9.claim: Ikrima asked Ibn Abbas whether silent people were saved because they disliked the wrongdoing and opposed the transgressors; Ibn Abbas gave him two coarse garments, signaling approval of that argument.
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r9.anchor: وفي رواية عكرمة قلت لابن عباس أي جعلني الله فداك ألا ترى أنهم كرهوا ما هم عليه وخالفوهم

TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r10.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects Ikrima's inference: although the silent group disliked the forbidden fishing and did not participate, they committed a graver sin by abandoning the duty to forbid wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r10.anchor: وقد أخطأ عكرمة فإن القوم وإن كانوا كرهوا فعلهم ولم يشاركوهم في الصيد المحرم لكنهم اقترفوا معصية هي أعظم من ذلك

TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r11.claim: The admonishers' words show they had not despaired of the warning's effect, so the duty to enjoin right remained; once they gave up, they withdrew, whereas the silent group stayed among the transgressors.
TABATABAI:7:161-171#2/r11.anchor: وكلامهم يدل على أن المقام لم يكن مقام اليأس

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r1.claim: The opening clause is conjoined to the earlier account of Sabbath violation and describes the righteous group’s circumstances and outcome amid persistent transgression.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r1.anchor: يَعْدُونَ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ cümlesine mâtuftur ve o karye ahâlisinin fısk ve ta‘addîde ve nasihat dinlememekteki mütemâdî ısrarlarıyla içlerindeki sulehânın hâl ve âkıbetlerini beyandır.

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r2.claim: The town had two broad groups: transgressing wrongdoers and a minority of religious, righteous people who could not restrain them.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r2.anchor: o karye ahâlisi iki kısım idi, bir kısmı fâsık mütecâvizler gürûhu, bir kısmı da dindar sulehâ cemaati idi ki bunlar ekalliyette kalmış

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r3.claim: The righteous themselves divided: one group eventually despaired and stopped admonishing, while another small group persisted.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r3.anchor: Bunlar da iki kısım olmuştu, bir kısım sulehâ uğraşmış, uğraşmış acı tatlı, zor kolay her yoldan giderek

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r4.claim: The group that stopped admonishing had tried every means, then despaired, withdrew, and ceased counseling out of hostility toward the wrongdoers.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r4.anchor: nihâyet bıkmış, me’yus olmuş, Allah’tan bu ahâliye bir belâ geleceğine karar vermiş, o halka buğzlarından dolayı nasihatten vazgeçmiş

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r5.claim: Although a minority beside the transgressors, this withdrawn righteous group was numerous and organized enough to count as a community.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r5.anchor: bunlar fâsıklara nisbeten az olmakla beraber yine bir ümmet denecek kadar bir kesreti hâiz idiler ve kendi aralarında bir ictimâ‘iyetleri var idi.

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r6.claim: A very small righteous group kept preaching despite hardship; the despairing group challenged them for counseling a people seemingly doomed to destruction or severe punishment.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r6.anchor: ekall-i kalîl diğer bir kısım sulehâ ise asla me’yus olmuyorlar, bütün mezâhim ü müşkilâta rağmen va‘z u nasihatle uğraşmaya devam ediyorlardı

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r7.claim: The despairing group wanted the persistent counselors to stop and leave the people alone, failing to see that abandoning a communal duty would make everyone sinful.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r7.anchor: bu suretle bunları nasihatten vazgeçirip halkı bütün bütün hâllerine bırakmayı tercih eylemişler ve böyle derken bir farz-ı kifâyenin umûmen terkiyle hepsinin âsim olacaklarını düşünememişlerdi.

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r8.claim: The persistent group first preached to have an excuse before God and avoid blame for neglecting the communal duty to forbid wrong while people remained alive.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r8.anchor: sırf Allah’a karşı mazeretimiz bulunmak, nehy ani’l-münker husûsunda indallah bir nevi taksir ve tefrit ile müttehem olmamaktır. Çünkü nehy ani’lmünker henüz ber-hayat olanlara son nefese kadar bir farz-ı kifâyedir.

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r9.claim: Their second reason was hope that the people might begin to fear God, even partly; despair is impermissible, and people’s future response is unknown before it occurs.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r9.anchor: İkincisi yeis dünyada hiçbir hususta câiz değildir.

ELMALILI:7:164-170/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r10.claim: Counsel is better than abandoning counsel: it may at least slow or soften wrongdoing and punishment, and if disaster is decreed, those who warned are excused before God.
ELMALILI:7:164-170/r10.anchor: Her hâlde nasihat terk-i nasihatten evlâdır. Nasihati bütün bütün bırakmakta hiçbir ümit yoktur. Fakat nasihate devamın hiç olmazsa birazcık olsun sakındırmaya sebep olması me’muldür.

BURHAN:v1p199/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p199/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p199/r5.claim: Al-Aʿrāf is Meccan except three verses, beginning with the command to ask about the town and extending through the verse about the mountain being raised.
BURHAN:v1p199/r5.anchor: سورة الأعراف مكية إلا ثلاث آيات

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: Sibawayh reads معذرة in قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم as a raised predicate: their admonition is an excuse to their Lord; if it meant a fresh apology, it would be accusative.
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.anchor: ومثله فى أنه على الابتداء وليس على فعل

NASHR:v2p272/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p272/r10.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v2p272/r10.claim: Hafs reads معذرة in the accusative.
NASHR:v2p272/r10.anchor: فروى حفص بالنصب، وقرأ الباقون بالرفع

NASHR:v2p272/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p272/r11.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p272/r11.claim: The remaining readers read معذرة in the nominative.
NASHR:v2p272/r11.anchor: فروى حفص بالنصب، وقرأ الباقون بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r1.claim: The apparent reading has three groups: transgressors, preachers, and a third group that neither sinned nor admonished; the questioners are distinct from those addressed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن القائل غير المقول لهم لم تعظون قوما فيكون ثلاث فرق اعتدوا وفرقة وعظت ونهت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r2.claim: An alternative report has only two groups: sinners and admonishers, with some sinners mockingly asking why they preach to people God will destroy or punish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r2.anchor: وروي أنهم كانوا فرقتين فرقة عصت وفرقة نهت ووعظت وأن جماعة من العاصية قالت للواعظة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the three-group account: the direct plural address “your Lord” and “they may fear” implies an audience separate from the questioners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والقول الأول أصوب ويؤيده الضمائر في قوله معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r4.claim: Muhlikuhum may mean removing them and purifying the land of them, or punishing them severely for persisting in disobedience; the excerpt begins but does not complete a further qualification about worldly punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p207/r4.anchor: ومعنى مهلكهم مخترمهم ومطهر الأرض منهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا لتماديهم في العصيان
